elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Paragraph 1(b) states "Contractor shall provide sufficient qualified personnel to perform the Services in a professional and workmanlike manner in accordance with industry standards" — a performance covenant, not a representation or warranty; the inserted warranty sentence warrants only conformity to "the requirements of this Agreement" for 30 days and contains no professional/workmanlike warranty. To meet this element the drafter would need an express "Contractor warrants that the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner" statement.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "each software deliverable included in the Works will conform in all material respects to its documentation".

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: Inserted period is "ninety (90) days following delivery" for software deliverables, not twelve (12) months.
Inserted Services warranty runs "for thirty (30) days following performance", short of 90 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "at Contractor's option, repair or replacement of the non-conforming software deliverable or Services".
Inserted: "or a refund of the fees paid for them".

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: Retained 5(a): Contractor "represents and warrants ... that Contractor's performance of the Services ... does not and shall not violate any applicable law, rule, or regulation". The "to its knowledge" qualifier weakens it below the preferred unqualified standard but an express legal-compliance warranty exists.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No anti-malicious-code warranty appears in Section 5, in paragraph 1(b), or in the inserted sentence; a separate "no viruses, malware or other malicious code" warranty would be required.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "for ninety (90) days following delivery, each software deliverable included in the Works will conform in all material respects to its documentation" — an express software-to-documentation warranty at the 90-day floor.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "for thirty (30) days following performance, the Services will conform to the requirements of this Agreement" — 30 days, meeting the floor.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Inserted remedy sentence expressly provides "repair or replacement of the non-conforming software deliverable or Services".
Inserted remedy sentence expressly provides "a refund of the fees paid for them".

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the single inserted sentence supplies a 90-day software-to-documentation warranty, a 30-day Services warranty, and repair/replacement or refund remedies, matching all four fallback elements in operative language.

Preferred level is incomplete: no express professional-and-workmanlike warranty (paragraph 1(b) is a covenant only), software period is 90 days rather than 12 months, Services period is 30 days rather than 90 days, and there is no no-malicious-code warranty.

The finding is correctly classified as a deviation: the original Section 5 warranties (legal compliance, authority/rights, non-infringement) contain no conformance warranty, no warranty period and no repair/replace/refund remedy, so the clause fails the fallback on material terms.

Minimality holds: the redline adds one concise sentence covering only the four fallback elements, deletes nothing, and adds no survival tail, expense allocation, notice procedure or extra damages categories. No disclaimer carve-out was needed because 5(e) expressly preserves "THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES IN THIS AGREEMENT", so the new warranty is not swallowed.

Intent preserved: retained warranties 5(a)-(c), the 1(b) performance covenant and 5(e) disclaimer remain coherent alongside the insertion; no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created ("Works", "Services" and "this Agreement" are all defined).
